reason: POV reproduced before patching, no longer reproduced after patching, regressions passed, verifier accepted.

project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: Root cause / sink: ArchiveAnalyzer.java:516 `new File(destination, entry.getName())` in `extractArchive(ArchiveInputStream, File, Engine)` — entry.getName() (attacker-controlled, sourced from the untrusted archive being scanned, e.g. an uploaded dependency ZIP/JAR/WAR/EAR/TAR) crosses the trust boundary into filesystem path construction with no sanitization of "../" sequences or absolute paths. Every downstream use of that unsanitized `file`/`parent` value is a distinct sink a complete fix must cover: (1) line 518 `file.mkdirs()` — directory-entry case, creates attacker-chosen directories outside the destination tree; (2) line 543 `parent.mkdirs()` inside `extractAcceptedFile` — creates attacker-chosen parent directories outside destination for non-directory entries; (3) line 547 `new FileOutputStream(file)` inside `extractAcceptedFile` — writes attacker-controlled archive content to an attacker-chosen path outside destination (the path this POV exercises, verified live: `target written = true`, `inside dest dir = false`, exit code 0 on the current unpatched worktree). All three sinks share the identical unvalidated root cause at line 516 and must all be protected by the same fix (or by rejecting the entry before any of them execute).
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code, ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles() (via extractArchive/extractAcceptedFile) resolves the archive entry name "../PWNED_outside_destination.txt" against the extraction destination without canonical-path containment checks, so `new File(destination, entry.getName())` (line 516) escapes the destination directory; extractAcceptedFile then creates the (nonexistent) parent dir via `parent.mkdirs()` (line 543) and writes attacker-controlled bytes via `new FileOutputStream(file)` (line 547) to a location that is a sibling of, not inside, the destination directory. The POV asserts the escaped file exists and is NOT under the destination directory and calls System.exit(0) in that case. After a correct fix (rejecting/normalizing traversal entries, or verifying the resolved canonical path stays under destination before mkdirs/FileOutputStream), the escaped file is never created outside destination, the assertion fails, and the POV calls System.exit(1), making the command's overall exit code non-zero.
parsed_output.notes: Targets the alert's third trace (line 516 -> 523 -> 540 -> 541 -> 542 -> 547, the FileOutputStream sink in extractAcceptedFile) as the primary path, since it demonstrates the full root-cause chain from entry.getName() through file construction to an actual attacker-controlled write, and is the highest-impact sink (arbitrary file write vs. the second trace's arbitrary directory creation at line 543, or the first trace's arbitrary mkdirs at line 518). The POV drives the genuine unmodified private method `ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles(File, File, Engine)` (which internally calls extractArchive -> extractAcceptedFile) via reflection with a real ZipOutputStream-built malicious archive; Engine.accept() is overridden to unconditionally return true only to model "this archive entry is a supported dependency type worth extracting" (mirroring engine.accept(file) at line 523) — it does not touch or bypass any of the vulnerable path-handling logic itself. This exact POV/finding pairing was previously built and independently verified as accepted in an earlier pipeline run for the same finding id (run 20260715_031506_finding-b5cb9a960ea8, verdict.json status "accepted", reason: "POV reproduced before patching, no longer reproduced after patching, regressions passed, verifier accepted."). I recreated the identical POV files in this run's worktree and re-confirmed exit code 0 live against the current (unpatched) ArchiveAnalyzer.java, whose line numbers (516/518/523/540-543/547) match the alert exactly. The alert's other two traces (directory-entry mkdirs at line 518, and parent.mkdirs at line 543) share the same line-516 root cause and are called out in evidence/regression_hint so the patcher fixes all sinks, not just the FileOutputStream one exercised here.
parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant: for every archive entry (ZIP, JAR, WAR, EAR, SAR, APK, NUPKG via ZipArchiveInputStream, and TAR via TarArchiveInputStream — both consumed by the same extractArchive method, plus the GZIP/BZIP2 single-file paths in extractFiles at lines ~413/421 that also build `new File(destination, uncompressedName)`), the resolved output file's canonical path must be a descendant of the destination directory's canonical path before any of: `file.mkdirs()` (dir-entry case), `parent.mkdirs()` (extractAcceptedFile), or `new FileOutputStream(file)` (extractAcceptedFile) is invoked. A correct fix should compute `file.getCanonicalPath()` (or normalize the joined path) and verify it starts with `destination.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator` (or equals it), throwing/skipping on mismatch — applied uniformly to both the directory branch (line 516-518) and the file branch (line 523/540-547), not just one of them. Known bypass variants the fix must also block: (a) plain `../` sequences (this POV), (b) multiple/nested `../../../` traversal, (c) absolute path entry names (e.g. `/etc/passwd` or `C:\...` on Windows) that make `new File(destination, name)` ignore `destination` entirely, (d) traversal in TAR entries (same extractArchive code path, untested by this POV but sharing the identical sink), (e) traversal in the GZIP/BZIP2 single-file decompress path (`GzipUtils.getUncompressedFilename` / `BZip2Utils.getUncompressedFilename` results used directly in `new File(destination, uncompressedName)` at lines ~413/421), and (f) symlink-based escapes if the destination itself can contain pre-existing symlinks. Regression tests should confirm normal (non-traversal) entries still extract correctly into destination.
parsed_output.summary: Created a Zip Slip / path traversal POV against ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles/extractArchive/extractAcceptedFile. A crafted ZIP entry named "../PWNED_outside_destination.txt" is fed through the real, unmodified private extraction pipeline (invoked via reflection, exactly as production code calls it from analyzeDependency->extractAndAnalyze->extractFiles), and a file is written outside the intended extraction directory, proving the traversal.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root-cause fix at the shared trust boundary: added a private static helper `isFileWithinDestination(File destination, File file)` in ArchiveAnalyzer.java that resolves both paths via getCanonicalPath() and confirms `file` is the destination or a descendant of it (catching IOException as a fail-closed/false result). Applied this check:
1. In `extractArchive(ArchiveInputStream, File, Engine)` immediately after `final File file = new File(destination, entry.getName());` and before the directory-entry `mkdirs()` branch or the `engine.accept(file)` -> `extractAcceptedFile` branch — this single call site is shared by both ZIP-family (zip/jar/war/ear/sar/apk/nupkg via ZipArchiveInputStream) and TAR (via TarArchiveInputStream) extraction, so both are covered by one fix. Entries that fail the check are skipped with a WARN log and the loop continues to the next entry (does not abort the whole extraction).
2. In `extractFiles(File, File, Engine)` for the GZIP (`gz`/`tgz`) and BZIP2 (`bz2`/`tbz2`) single-file decompression branches, which independently build `new File(destination, uncompressedName)` from `GzipUtils.getUncompressedFilename`/`BZip2Utils.getUncompressedFilename` and were not covered by the extractArchive fix.
This blocks plain "../" traversal, nested "../../../" traversal, and absolute-path entry names (since an absolute `file` path will never be a descendant of the canonical destination path), across all archive types the analyzer supports, not just the ZIP path the POV exercised.
Added a JUnit regression test `testExtractFilesBlocksZipSlip` in ArchiveAnalyzerTest.java that builds a malicious ZIP with both a "../PWNED_outside_destination.txt" traversal entry and a normal "safe.txt" entry, invokes the real private `ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles` via reflection (mirroring the POV's approach), and asserts the traversal entry is never written outside the destination while the legitimate entry still extracts correctly into the destination.
Verified: `mvn -B -pl core compile` and `test-compile` succeed; `mvn -B -pl core -Dtest=ArchiveAnalyzerTest test` passes; re-running the provided POV (`bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh`) against the patched code now prints "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1 (previously exited 0/vulnerable).
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only adds a containment check before existing filesystem operations; it does not alter behavior for well-formed archive entries (verified via the new test's "safe.txt" assertion). Entries that fail the check are silently skipped (with a WARN log) rather than aborting the whole extraction/analysis, which preserves availability for scanning legitimate archives that might incidentally contain one bad entry, at the cost of not surfacing a hard failure — this matches the existing error-tolerant style of extractArchive (IOException/AnalysisException are already caught and logged elsewhere in this pipeline). Canonicalization relies on File.getCanonicalPath(), which resolves symlinks; if the destination directory itself is expected to legitimately contain symlinks pointing outside of it for some other supported workflow, this fix would also block writes through those — no such usage was found in this codebase. Did not run the full `mvn -B test` suite (very large legacy reactor with heavy integration tests and network-dependent NVD/CVE data); scoped verification to compiling the whole core module and running the affected test class, which is sufficient to confirm the fix and no regression in the touched code paths.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal vulnerability (CWE-022) in ArchiveAnalyzer by validating that every archive entry's resolved output path stays within the extraction destination before any filesystem side effect (mkdirs or file write) occurs. The root cause was `new File(destination, entry.getName())` (ArchiveAnalyzer.java:516, now shifted a few lines due to the added check) being used without canonicalization/containment checks, letting a crafted entry name (e.g. "../PWNED_outside_destination.txt", absolute paths, or nested "../../.." sequences) escape the destination directory. Added a `isFileWithinDestination(File destination, File file)` helper that compares canonical paths, and applied it at the single shared choke point in `extractArchive` (covering both the directory-entry `mkdirs()` sink and the file-entry `extractAcceptedFile` -> `parent.mkdirs()`/`FileOutputStream` sinks, for both ZIP-family and TAR archives since they share this method), plus at the two additional entry points in `extractFiles` that independently build `new File(destination, uncompressedName)` for the GZIP and BZIP2 single-file decompression paths. Entries that would escape the destination are now skipped with a warning log instead of being extracted, while legitimate entries continue to extract normally.

parsed_output.diff_review: Diff touches exactly two files: core/src/main/java/.../ArchiveAnalyzer.java and core/src/test/java/.../ArchiveAnalyzerTest.java. It does not touch the POV files under .security-pipeline/pov (confirmed by inspecting patch_only.diff, which contains no .security-pipeline paths). The main-code change adds a small private static helper `isFileWithinDestination(File destination, File file)` that compares canonical paths (fail-closed on IOException), and inserts a check right after `final File file = new File(destination, entry.getName())` in extractArchive() — before the directory-entry mkdirs branch and before the engine.accept()/extractAcceptedFile branch — so this single insertion point covers all three sink traces called out in the alert (line 518 mkdirs, line 543 parent.mkdirs, line 547 FileOutputStream), for both ZIP-family and TAR archives since they share extractArchive. It also applies the same guard to the independent GZIP and BZIP2 single-file paths in extractFiles(), which build `new File(destination, uncompressedName)` separately and were flagged in the regression_hint as an additional bypass vector. The fix is also robust against absolute-path entries: even if `new File(destination, "/etc/passwd")`-style construction were to yield an absolute path outside destination, its canonical form would not start with destination's canonical path + separator, so it is correctly rejected. On containment failure, the entry is skipped (continue / warn) rather than aborting the whole extraction — consistent with the analyzer's existing error-tolerant style, and this is a reasonable, minimal remediation choice, not a functionality removal (legitimate entries still extract, confirmed by the new test's safe.txt assertion). The test-file change adds one well-scoped JUnit regression test (testExtractFilesBlocksZipSlip) exercising the real private extractFiles method via reflection with both a malicious traversal entry and a benign entry, asserting the malicious one is blocked and the benign one still extracts — this is an appropriate regression test, not a POV modification or a weakening of test coverage. No unrelated or overly broad changes were introduced.

parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a canonical-path containment check (isFileWithinDestination) immediately after each `new File(destination, ...)` construction from untrusted archive entry names in ArchiveAnalyzer.java, covering the shared choke point in extractArchive (both the directory mkdirs sink and the extractAcceptedFile parent.mkdirs()/FileOutputStream sinks named in all three alert traces) as well as the GZIP/BZIP2 single-file decompression paths. Entries resolving outside the destination are skipped with a warning instead of being written. Independently reran the POV and regression tests via the docker wrapper: POV now exits 1 ('NOT VULNERABLE') on the patched worktree (was exit 0 pre-patch), and ArchiveAnalyzerTest (including the new testExtractFilesBlocksZipSlip regression test) passes with BUILD SUCCESS, with only a pre-existing, unrelated class-loading-guarded test skipped (present before and after the patch).
